result.eligibility: VACANT: Likely, but not confirmed. Every 2022-2026 MLS listing calls it land (R1, 34,412 sf / 0.79 ac). They say water, sewer and power are on site and suggest a detached ADU as a possible use. But Trulia's record for 4269 Hillside shows a 1946 house (3 bed, 3 bath, 1,500 sf) on a 1.68-ac parcel, sold for $1,000,000 on 2/28/2023. The Coldwell Banker listing (NDP2511605) says tax records show the 4269 address 'due to a previous submission for a lot split'. If that split was never recorded, the legal lot may still be the 1.68-ac parent with a house on it. That would exceed SB 1123's 1.5-ac limit and would not be vacant. Get a title report or recorded parcel map before relying on 0.79 ac. SIZE/UNITS: 0.79 ac is under 1.5 ac, and 8 units is under the 10-unit cap, if the 0.79-ac lot is a legal lot. COASTAL ZONE: Probably inside it. The site is on the north shore of Agua Hedionda Lagoon. City staff report CDP 99-24 (a house on adjacent Highland Dr) says a single-family home there is 'within the City's Coastal Zone' and needs a Coastal Development Permit. SB 684/1123 do not override the Coastal Act, so a CDP would likely be needed and the approval would not be purely ministerial (it could be appealed). Confirm on the city's coastal zone map. VERY HIGH FIRE HAZARD SEVERITY ZONE: Not determined. Carlsbad has adopted CAL FIRE's updated map, which includes moderate, high and very high zones. Being in a very high zone is an SB 684/1123 exclusion unless mitigation applies. The listing describes the lot as 'elevated and wooded' next to the lagoon, so this needs a parcel check. SUBSTANTIALLY SURROUNDED BY URBAN USES: Not verified. The site is inside an established single-family area (Highland Dr, Park Dr, Sunnyhill Dr homes), so it probably passes. Lagoon-side open space on the perimeter could matter for the 75%-of-perimeter test. SLOPE: Not measured. 'Elevated and wooded' suggests slope. Carlsbad's Hillside Development rules (CMC 21.95) apply where slopes are 15% or more and the elevation difference exceeds 15 ft. Expect grading, retaining-wall and tree costs. CARLSBAD IMPLEMENTATION: Yes. The city publishes Information Bulletin IB-166 on ministerial small-lot subdivisions under SB 684 and SB 1123, and Form P-48, an SB-1123 eligibility checklist. Council Policy 44 (Small Lot Guidelines) is an existing design policy. I could not retrieve the text of IB-166 or P-48, so any local objective standards or limits are not confirmed.
